page: Microsoft Azure E64-32s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained-core architecture designed for memory-intensive workloads requiring fewer licensed CPU cores. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores alongside 512 GB of system memory, yielding a high ratio of 16 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include 260 MB of L3 cache as well as Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets for accelerated matrix operations and vector processing. The configuration features zero GPUs and includes no local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on remote managed storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate solid throughput across compute and memory subsystems. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved strong results with a single-core score of 2,143 and a multi-core score of 17,375. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth demonstrated top-quartile performance, reaching 246.92 GB/sec for reads and 141.39 GB/sec for writes. The platform also registered high static web serving throughput at 44.87 GB/sec and rapid single-threaded gzip compression at 31.38 GB/sec. Standard computational workloads placed in the median bracket, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 31,965.7 and Redis achieving 43.96 million SET operations per second.

The constrained vCPU allocation paired with 512 GB of RAM delivers significant cost efficiency for database engines and enterprise software where licensing costs scale strictly by active core count. By allocating 16 GB of memory per vCPU, systems can maintain large in-memory caches without incurring excessive per-core licensing expenses. However, the lack of attached local storage mandates network-attached storage integration, introducing external I/O considerations. The E64-32s_v6 is optimal for enterprise relational databases, large-scale in-memory analytics, Redis caching clusters, and ETL data pipeline processing.
